neighbours.label: In English, the modal 'can' (strongest as 'you can', weaker 'could') opening a main clause right after a reason clause (since, because, as, or ', so') that says a thing's feature makes an action easy or safe, e.g. 'Since the battery lasts all week, you can leave the charger at home'; quiet for 'can' with no reason before it, for negatives (cannot, could not, must not), for purpose 'so that ... could', and for questions 'Can you ...?'.
neighbours.short: 'you can' licensed by a preceding reason (since/because/so)
fire: Because the jacket is fully waterproof, you can hike through the storm without worry.
As the pan has a nonstick coating, you can cook eggs with almost no oil.
The app saves your progress automatically, so you can close it at any time.
Since the lid locks tightly, you can toss the container in your bag.
Because the blade is so sharp, you can slice tomatoes paper thin.
As the bridge was reinforced last year, trucks can cross it safely now.
The tent sets up in two minutes, so you can pitch it even after dark.
Since the dough freezes well, you can make a double batch and save half.
quiet: The battery lasts all week, and the charger fits in a small pocket.
You can leave the charger at home this weekend.
Because the jacket is not waterproof, you cannot hike through the storm.
As the pan has a nonstick coating, it needs only a gentle wash.
Can you close the app before you leave the room?
Since the lid is cracked, you must not toss the container in your bag.
She sharpened the blade so that she could slice tomatoes thin.
As the bridge was reinforced last year, the town held a small ceremony.

predictions: Near misses stay quiet; fire items vary a lot with the reason's wording (probes ran 0.08-0.77), so the median-0.20 bar is the risk. Blind test written by a label-only second author.
